content:
Mary King’s Close tops a new ranking of the country’s spookiest tourist attractions, with York Minster and London’s Theatre Royal, Drury Lane also making the top three

Searches for “most haunted locations in the world” have surged by 5,000% as Halloween approaches, according to research cited by Psychic World, which has ranked the UK’s tourist attractions based on reported supernatural activity.

Edinburgh’s Mary King’s Close takes the top spot, scoring 9.75 out of 10 in the study. The historic underground streets are associated with centuries of ghost stories, including sightings of a lonely little girl known as Annie.

The research analysed thousands of ghost reports, assessing the number of allegedly haunted sites near each attraction alongside mentions of supernatural encounters.

The UK’s 15 most haunted attractions

  1. Mary King’s Close, Edinburgh — 9.75
  2. Theatre Royal, Drury Lane, London — 9.22
  3. York Minster, York — 8.95
  4. Gloucester Cathedral, Gloucestershire — 8.65
  5. Pluckley Village, Kent — 8.38
  6. Newcastle Castle, Newcastle — 8.27
  7. Edinburgh Dungeon, Edinburgh — 8.17
  8. Dudley Castle, West Midlands — 7.85
  9. Shepton Mallet Prison, Somerset — 7.84
  10. Edinburgh Castle, Edinburgh — 7.64
  11. Chislehurst Caves, Kent — 7.45
  12. Warwick Castle, Warwickshire — 7.39
  13. Arundel Castle, West Sussex — 7.17
  14. Stirling Castle, Stirling — 6.30
  15. Margam Castle, Port Talbot — 6.23

Edinburgh features three times in the top 10, making it the most frequently represented city in the rankings. Scotland also accounts for four of the 15 attractions listed.

Mary King’s Close is renowned for its stories of unexplained activity, with reported experiences including strange noises, doors allegedly slamming on their own and a clock said to repeatedly stop at 4.15am. Its most famous ghost story concerns Annie, a young girl said to haunt the historic site.

London’s Theatre Royal, Drury Lane, takes second place with a score of 9.22. The West End venue is associated with the ghost of actor William Terriss, who was murdered in 1897. His spirit has reportedly been seen wearing a grey suit and white gloves.

York Minster ranks third, scoring 8.95 and with 39 allegedly haunted sites identified nearby. York’s long history and its reputation as one of Europe’s most haunted cities have helped cement its place among the country’s most talked-about locations for ghost stories. Reported encounters around the cathedral include the sound of children singing and laughing in a nearby passage.

In fourth place, Gloucester Cathedral scores 8.65, with 16 haunted sites within 500 metres. Among the local tales is a story of a hunched-back ghost said to haunt a pub and cellar, reportedly knocking the elbows of drinkers and leaving furniture rearranged overnight.

Rounding out the top five is Pluckley Village in Kent, which scores 8.38. The village is associated with numerous ghost stories and is often described as one of England’s most haunted locations. Among its best-known legends is that of Lady Dering, whose ghost is said to appear in the churchyard of St Nicholas.

Places clearly even Yvette Fielding would need two pairs of knickers before visiting.
